decisions.reason: The firm has kept Product A on its own page across two years, signaling visible commitment and enough sunk development cost in a long-cycle space market to justify persistence despite no reported win yet.

Product B has both sustained standalone promotion and a publicly highlighted ESA HERA flight success, making withdrawal very unlikely for a large German optics firm that has already validated and publicized the product.

Product C remains on its own page and fits the firm's announced space-sensor direction, so management is likely to continue backing it and treat any weak commercial traction as temporary given long procurement cycles.

Product D has lower visible commitment because it is only mentioned rather than fully featured, but the firm is still likely to retain it for now because space-qualified sensor investments are costly and recent disappointments can be framed as early-market timing issues.
As a 2024 launch with its own page, Product E carries fresh public commitment and little time for a fair market test, which under escalation of commitment strongly favors continued support.

Product F is less prominently presented than some others, but because it is very new and sits close to the firm's space-navigation theme, management is likely to keep it and attribute limited evidence so far to the normal delay of mission-driven demand.
